parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal binary-sex document order, passport-marker restrictions upheld in Nov 2025, visa cable directing refusal on document discrepancy with possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and federal facility exclusion create universal border/facility exposure. The specific state repealed its birth-certificate bathroom law in 2017 and currently has no facility criminalisation, which mitigates state-level exposure, but a 2025 revival bill is unresolved. State law retains original sex on amended certificates, bans minor care and trans girls' sports, lacks gender-identity hate-crime and statewide private-sector protections, and covers only about 30% of population locally. National custody reports of hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse increase severity if detained. Courts and litigation provide partial, not reliable, recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary-sex definition, X-marker passports stopped for nationals, Supreme Court allowed restrictions in Nov 2025; visa cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passports confiscated/blocked reported, some stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs pending. No documented visitor-specific exemption.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport mismatch at visa/entry can trigger refusal, investigation, detention and custody exposure; state amended certificates retaining original sex compound document inconsistency for residents and any state ID sought.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men. State funds barred for transition care in prison.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Earlier prison LGBTQ executive order rescinded; no documented protective placement protocol for visitors. Courts and suits challenge orders, several enjoined, but no documented custody remedy operating.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration detention converts a document/facility discrepancy into birth-sex-aligned custody, medication denial and documented abuse risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State layer currently has no statute barring facility use matching identity and no criminalisation after 2017 repeal; 2025 revival bill keeps status open.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State repeal documented in 2017; no state facility ban or criminal offence documented. Federal ban remains operative exposure in federal/funded facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection does not cancel federal facilities, entry screening, or federal custody rules; traveller must navigate different rules by building owner/ funder.

care_services.exposure: State laws effective 2023 ended puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18; 2025 law bars state funds for minor and prisoner transition care. National orders target minor care and public insurance. Visitor seeking continuity faces denial/delay.
care_services.protection: No documented visitor care-access protection or continuity protocol. Some national orders blocked/enjoined, status uncertain at travel time.
care_services.interaction: Care denial is more severe for a minor traveller and for a detained adult whose hormone medication is removed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders frame gender identity as ideology to remove, direct investigation/prosecution over school pronoun use for minors, military and sports bans, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising groups described as radically pro-transgender. Poll: 66% support assigned-sex document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling remains; several orders enjoined and challenges pending. No state bias-crime coverage for gender identity or sexual orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises police discretion at borders, facilities and schools, while litigation uncertainty makes enforcement unpredictable.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor care banned, assigned-male-at-birth sports ban, school law requires parental notification on name/pronoun request for K-4 and bars gender-identity instruction, federal order directs criminal investigation of staff facilitating social transition. Travelling minor cannot access care or compete consistently.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented protection for visiting minors/guardians; conversion therapy on minors may not be publicly funded by state executive order, which does not restore care access.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor faces care denial, sports exclusion, and school-context investigation risk if minor enrols or is placed in school activities.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime coverage for gender identity/sexual orientation; statewide private employment/housing/public-accommodations protection absent, local ordinances cover about 30% of population by residence in largest city and one county. One first-known bathroom trespass arrest nationally in 2025 illustrates enforcement elsewhere.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime law exists; local ordinances in some jurisdictions explicitly cover gender identity from 2022. No documented pattern of police profiling/extortion in this state dossier, and no documented visitor-specific attack pattern.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor outside covered municipalities has thin recourse after assault or service denial; police response may vary by locality.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; Supreme Court allowed marker restrictions; several orders enjoined but scope changes. 2025 bathroom bill text/enforcement not established; county application of dual-marker certificates not established.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, civil-liberties litigation, national courts, and local ordinances provide some avenues, but no documented swift visitor remedy for entry refusal, facility exclusion, or custody harm.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved federal litigation plus open state legislation means the operative rule at travel may be more restrictive than the state facility position documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal exclusion at entry/documents with humiliation and poor appeals, but this case lacks routine detention without charge as the central visitor outcome and has a state with no current facility ban, so it sits slightly above 0.35 despite documented custody abuse if detained.

Below 0.55-B because border screening here can lead to refusal and a possible permanent fraud finding, federal facilities are restricted, custody abuse and medication removal are documented, and state recourse for bias, housing and public accommodations is absent statewide.

Well below 0.75-C: that anchor has accepted matching passports, respectful inspection and tribunal compensation; here documents are restricted by sex assigned at birth, entry refusal is directed on discrepancy, and remedies are litigation-dependent rather than reliably compensatory.

parsed.synthesis: State facility repeal is a real mitigation, but it does not neutralise the federal document, entry, facilities and custody regime. The traveller's decisive encounters—visa/entry discrepancy, federal buildings, any detention, and for minors care/sports—are governed by restrictive national rules with documented severity and uncertain judicial relief. Absent statewide bias-crime and private-sector protections, local ordinances help only a minority of locations. The interaction of document mismatch with investigation and birth-sex custody is the highest-risk pathway.
